message_source_quote: A self-authored stance-contrast steering vector, inspired by but distinct from Raman et al.'s White-Bear Steering (WBS)
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (2026) showed a think / don't-think stance vector from WSB's `directed_modulation` items lifts association pass@10 from 0.14 to 0.83 on Qwen3.5-4B. I asked whether the same axis can be recovered from **self-written prompts** with different concepts and wordings, making the method portable without the benchmark family.
rationale: Both documents identify Raman et al. (2026) / White-Bear Steering as the source the method is built on, explicitly noting the method is a variant/portable reproduction using self-authored prompts instead of WSB's directed_modulation items. Both state the same novelty claim (recovering the stance axis from independently authored prompts to make it benchmark-independent) and the same cosine similarity (0.96) and dosing rationale, so there is no material difference between the two accounts.
